Hi Morgan — thanks for the clear ask and the SIG artifact. Short answer: yes, we can support a customer-scoped log retention extension with guarded access and contractual amendment. There are a few implementation and evidence items to align on. High-level options:

1) Short-term, account-bound retention window (per-customer TTL override) — keep logs for 180 days in encrypted object storage with strict IAM controls and access logging.
2) Log escrow snapshot on a recurring cadence (weekly/biweekly) held in an encrypted escrow bucket with HMACed manifests — access via an approved request and multi-owner approval.
3) Hybrid: keep application-level request traces for 90 days and escrow aggregated forensic packages for 180 days.

Compensating controls we propose:
- Customer-scoped KMS key (optional) or Redwood-managed KMS with customer separation.
- Access approver workflow (security + account owner) with SSO and step-up MFA.
- Immutable manifests and deletion certificate signed at TTL expiry.

Neha (cc) will confirm technical constraints and where we can provide exported evidence (deletion certs, manifests, audit logs). Rishi (cc) will scope contract language for an amendment / SLA addendum and whether the change needs legal sign-off beyond standard PO.

Can you confirm the exact log classes you need (request headers, request/response payloads, KV cache events, system traces) and whether PII is present in the examples you attached? Also share whether your auditors require an independent attestation for the retention process or whether Redwood's SOC2 report plus our deletion certificates are sufficient.

I can put together a proposed controls doc and a timeline for delivery once we have the log classes.

Camila / Morgan — quick technical note from infra/security:

We can support per-account TTL overrides for the following logical artifacts:
- request metadata (timestamps, headers, route, model id) — yes, standard retention extension supported.
- request/response payloads — possible, but only for encrypted escrow and with explicit contract and data classification; we will treat payloads with PII as ineligible for extended storage unless the customer provides a customer-managed key.
- KV cache artifacts — no; these are ephemeral and not written to archival storage.
- system-level traces (kernel/infra diagnostics) — we can include aggregated diagnostic bundles rather than raw traces to control exposure.

Evidence we can produce:
- periodic retention manifests (sha256) and signed deletion certificates at expiry.
- access audit trail (who requested export, approver, timestamp) exportable as CSV.
- configuration snapshot showing TTL override and associated policy id.

Estimated delivery timeline after contract commitment:
- Controls document and evidence templates: 4 business days.
- Engineering enablement for account TTL override (if not already on Dedicated): 7–10 business days after PO and JIRA ticket.
- First retention manifest and escrow delivery: within 14 days of enablement.

If Morgan can confirm log classes and whether payloads contain regulated PII, we can finalize the controls doc and templates.

-Neha
Principal Security Engineer\Redwood Inference
